terms.gloss: sit with folded hands, sit idle
evidence: Traupman 99: compressīs manibus sedēre, sit on one’s hands
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “with the hands folded, i.e. to be unemployed, at leisure” (a proverb).

terms.grammar: porrigō with digitum; nē … quidem round the noun
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. digitus: “not to give one’s self the least trouble”

terms.comment: Traupman’s form on p. 98; on p. 99 he gives compressīs manibus, which is the phrase Lewis & Short cites from Livy. Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections.

sources: Lewis & Short: comprimo · Lewis & Short: digitus · Lewis & Short: porrigo
